tagline: Innovative medicines that make a difference
hero_kpi_rationale: Tagrisso is AstraZeneca's leading oncology revenue driver, generating $7,254 million in 2025 and representing approximately 30% of oncology segment revenues. This key blockbuster anchors an innovation-focused portfolio in oncology.

kpis.name: Leading drug revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by the company's best-selling medicine, here Tagrisso in oncology.
kpis.description: Tagrisso (osimertinib) is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer. Its double-digit growth demonstrates strong continued clinical adoption.
kpis.signal: Tagrisso remains the oncology pillar despite competition

kpis.name: Phase 3 R&D pipeline
kpis.explanation: Number of molecules in Phase 3 development, the final stage before regulatory approval.
kpis.description: The 6-K mentions positive results for four Phase 3 programs, including two new molecular entities (NMEs): tozorakimab and efzimfotase alfa. This strengthens pipeline visibility over the medium term.
kpis.signal: Four Phase 3 programs with positive results since late 2025

kpis.name: Adjusted operating margin
kpis.explanation: Profit margin after operating costs, excluding exceptional items.
kpis.description: Operating margin improved significantly in 2025 driven by strong growth in high-margin sales, notably in oncology and specialty medicines. Operating profit of $13,743 million on total revenue of $58,739 million equals 23.4%.
kpis.signal: Strong operating margin improvement driven by blockbuster growth

kpis.name: R&D investments as percentage of revenue
kpis.explanation: Share of research and development spending in total revenue.
kpis.description: AstraZeneca maintains a high and growing R&D rate ($14,232 million / $58,739 million equals 24.2%), typical of major pharmaceutical innovators, to fuel its pipeline in oncology, CVRM and immunology.
kpis.signal: Strong commitment to innovation with increasing R&D spend

kpis.name: Vaccines and Immunotherapies segment revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from vaccines and specialized immunology treatments.
kpis.description: The Vaccines & Immune Therapies segment declined 20% in 2025, primarily due to falls in Synagis and Beyfortus sales linked to seasonality and post-pandemic demand. Beyfortus: $281 million, Synagis: $292 million, FluMist: $272 million.

kpis.name: Free cash flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated after all operating and capital expenditures.
kpis.description: FCF advanced in line with revenue growth and margin improvement, supporting dividends and strategic acquisitions.
kpis.signal: Strong free cash flow growth supports shareholder returns and strategic investments

kpis.name: Total assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €114.07 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Total debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €29.15 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Recent regulatory approvals
kpis.explanation: Number of regulatory approvals obtained in major regions since end of 2025.
kpis.description: These approvals cover multiple medicines, notably in oncology and specialty diseases, and open new commercial pathways to strengthen the therapeutic portfolio position.
kpis.signal: Fourteen regulatory approvals since Q4 2025 results

kpis.name: Recent positive Phase 3 results
kpis.explanation: Number of positive Phase 3 results published recently, notably for new medicines.
kpis.description: Among these, two new molecular entities (NMEs): tozorakimab (immunology) and efzimfotase alfa (specialty disease), which could become future blockbusters and strengthen the medium-term pipeline.
kpis.signal: Four Phase 3 programs achieved positive results

risks.title: Drug pipeline failure or delay
risks.score_rationale: Central position in the 10-K, strong language (failure, adversely affect, critical), stable trend, high weight because linked to the core of R&D activity and future growth.

risks.title: Strict regulation and uncertain approval
risks.score_rationale: Frequent and detailed mention, concerned language (refuse to approve, unpredictable), stable trend, key category for any pharmaceutical player.

risks.title: Pricing and market access pressures
risks.score_rationale: Important position, language marked by pressure (increasing cost-containment, pricing pressures), upward trend, high weight due to direct impact on profitability.

risks.title: Cybersecurity threats to sensitive data
risks.score_rationale: Alarming language (increasingly sophisticated, malicious AI use), reinforced position, upward trend, critical category due to value of R&D and medical data.

risks.title: Dependence on critical external suppliers
risks.score_rationale: Explicit and repeated mention, language of dependence (heavily reliant, difficult to substitute), stable trend, major operational impact on supply chain.

risks.title: Risks related to AI use
risks.score_rationale: New risk highlighted, cautious language (amplify biased, unreliable, regulatory scrutiny), upward trend, growing weight with AI adoption in R&D and medical decision-making.

risks.title: Counterfeit and illicit drug trafficking
risks.score_rationale: Concerned language (loss of public confidence, direct risk to patient safety), clear position, stable trend, high reputational and health impact.

risks.title: Commercial difficulties in emerging markets
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of specific risks, language of vulnerability (more challenging, inadequate protection), stable trend, significant regional weight for growth.

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence was found in the provided 10-K/20-F.
